recentItems.title: Why AI shouldn’t decide our future | Maks Giordano | TEDxBerlin
recentItems.description:
For thirty years, Maks Giordano helped companies find faster, smarter, creative paths into the future. Then AI arrived and raised a question he could not ignore: when machines become extraordinary at optimization, what remains uniquely human?

Drawing on a forgotten 1966 “documentary about the future,” Keith Jarrett’s broken piano, the birth of punk, and the strange history of human discovery, Maks explores the one thing no machine can do for us: decide what is worth pursuing in the first place. 

In a world obsessed with speed, this talk asks a different question: What deserves the speed? Maks Giordano is a digital creative strategist and innovation specialist with more than 30 years of experience leading innovation projects for iconic brands. He works at the intersection of exponential technologies and practical innovation, recognised both for his thinking on generative AI and for the hands-on work of applying it to transform industries and business models.

He has served as a management board member and Head of Innovation at ProSiebenSat.1, co-founded iconmobile (Exit to WPP) and Nunatak, and led the digital unit at MetaDesign. He also ran kyte's European operations, working with clients including Lady Gaga. Nominated as Entrepreneur of the Year by Ernst & Young, Maks is known for identifying the technologies that will matter and reading their impact across very different industries. He published two books, teaches Innovation Management and Entrepreneurship as an associate professor and holds an MBA from the University of St. Gallen. His current work, including a new book on "Innovation Alchemy" (Harriman House, 2027), examines what keeps people relevant as machines grow more capable: the human wandering, taste, and intuition that do not transfer easily to a model. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Growing Up Without Growing Apart | Dr. Valerie Woo | TEDxHSRW
recentItems.description:
What happens when growing up changes not just the child, but the parent too? In this personal and emotional talk, Valerie Woo explores what happens as young adults begin choosing lives of their own while their parents learn to step back, trust, and find a new way to stay connected.
Filmed and edited by Fotocinema (Arkadiusz Tomala). Dr. Valerie Woo is a pediatric dentist, entrepreneur, speaker, and proud daughter of Filipino immigrants. Through her work and personal story, she explores what it means to grow, lead, and become yourself in seasons of change. On the TEDxHSRW stage, Valerie will share the heart behind Half Nester, a concept born from her own life long before motherhood. Through that lens, she speaks to the in-between space so many students know well: between home and independence, family expectations and personal identity, ambition and belonging. With warmth, honesty, and insight, Valerie invites the audience to rethink what it means to be limitless, not by doing more or balancing everything perfectly, but by finding their own rhythm and realizing that becoming yourself is not a betrayal of where you come from. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What if the only limit was…you haven’t told your story yet? | Dr. Pradeep Ghosh | TEDxHSRW
recentItems.description:
Before a human recruiter reads a single word, an algorithm may already have said no. Most of us conclude we weren't good enough. After eight years of mentoring young professionals, Pradeep sees a different gap: not skills, but visibility. Through two short stories, a student from Montenegro and a master's student from India, he shows how they moved forward without a perfect CV. What changed things was one person who knew their story, understood it, and chose to help. Germans call it "Vitamin B." Pradeep calls it recognition, and it starts with being willing to be seen. At TEDxHSRW, he makes the case that in an age when algorithms decide who gets seen, the story you haven't yet told might be the most powerful thing you own. 
Filmed and edited by Fotocinema (Arkadiusz Tomala). Dr. Pradeep Ghosh's journey abroad as a young student began with strangers who welcomed him like family - a kindness that showed him how a single human story can open doors that no credential ever could. Today, as a physicist and Head of International Cooperations at FAIR, near Frankfurt, one of Europe's largest Big Science projects, he carries that same belief into science diplomacy: that breakthroughs aren't only about technology, but about people working together.

A returning TEDx speaker - having taken the stage at TEDxTUDarmstadt in November 2025, Pradeep has spent eight years coaching over 850 young professionals through career transitions, watching the same pattern repeat: the people who moved forward were rarely the most qualified. They were the ones who finally told their story.
At TEDxHSRW, he makes the case that in an age when algorithms decide who gets seen, the story you haven't yet told might be the most powerful thing you own This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. recentItems.title: Prioritizing family quality time over screen time | Giovanni Carlozzi | TEDxMiramar Youth
recentItems.description:
NOTE FROM TED: This talk only represents the speaker’s personal views and understanding of technology and addiction. This TEDx event was independently organized by volunteers by and for a youth audience. The guidelines we give TEDx organizers are described in more detail here: http://storage.ted.com/tedx/manuals/tedx_content_guidelines.pdf

Later than most parents think: Giovanni Carlozzi went through middle school without a phone and credits that with his confidence and people skills. While his friends had devices and social media, he spent his free time deep sea fishing and camping on islands in the Florida Keys with his family. He didn’t understand his parents’ rules until he noticed classmates who found the outdoors boring and kids glued to their phones at their own birthday parties. His parents also pushed him to greet adults and start conversations first, a habit he says put him on the TEDx stage. For parents deciding when to hand over a phone, and teens who think they’re missing out, Giovanni makes the case for growing up in an online world with offline parents.

This talk addresses: What happens when parents limit screen time? Kids without phones. Screen time and family bonding. Raising kids without social media. Teen screen time. Youth. Connection. Communication.

Part of the 2026 TEDxMiramar Youth Showcase: Growing Up Online.

 Giovanni Carlozzi is a student, wrestler, and DJ. He is also involved in church and Toastmaster Youth Leadership. He has traveled to 3 continents so far. He has an affinity for water sports, exploring the culinary world, and mastering music production and DJing.
His main project is sharing ideas worth encouraging and inspiring positive leadership skills to youth by participating and engaging in talks, feeding the homeless, and outreach with the elderly. Giovanni’s passion is fueled by his core beliefs and values with the importance on discipline and determination. He believes the focus on technology could use a closer observation. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Who knows you are here today? | Ranika Koneru | TEDxHSRW
recentItems.description:
Ranika has spent years inside healthcare systems, from running weight loss clinics in the U.S. to the Netherlands, and kept seeing the same gap between protocols and the people they were meant to help. In this talk, she shares that story and the science behind it with leaders, parents, and anyone who has cared for someone else. What’s eroding our health, our teams, and our families was never a discipline problem; it was always a disconnection problem.
Filmed and edited by Fotocinema (Arkadiusz Tomala). Ranika Koneru has spent years inside the systems meant to help people heal, and watched them fall short in the same quiet way every time. From running weight loss clinics in the U.S. to starting Origynz Longevity in the Netherlands, she kept finding the same distance between the protocols and the people inside them. 

Today she brings that story, and the science behind it, to leaders, parents, and anyone who has ever tried to take care of someone else. 
Because what’s slowly eroding our health, our teams, and our families was never a discipline problem. It was always a disconnection problem. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The shape you never chose is running your day | Aleksandra Kireeva | TEDxHSRW
recentItems.description:
Every system you move through was shaped by someone who is no longer there, for a world that has already changed. That's what a coffee shop has in common with a startup or university. 
We treat these shapes as the way things are and work inside them until the costs become too high. Aleks Kireeva on how to see the shape you inherited, and why you have the power to redesign it.
Filmed and edited by Fotocinema (Arkadiusz Tomala). Aleks Kireeva is a senior commercial operator who has spent fifteen years rebuilding operations at European fintechs and B2B SaaS companies. She currently leads Commercial Analytics for a €1.5 billion vertical at Delivery Hero, after earlier roles at Billie, Smava, and Neugelb, Commerzbank's digital subsidiary.
Her thesis is that companies aren't machines, even though we keep designing them like they are. The constraints that look permanent inside organisations: the queues, the silos, the rules everyone has accepted as "just how things work here", are almost always design choices someone made. Someone else can change them.
Aleks is Berlin-based, speaks five languages, and was named a Women in Tech Global Role Model in 2024.
Her TEDxHSRW talk is "Your Company Is an Organism - Stop Treating It Like a Machine." This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: When AI Makes Thinking Optional | Winston Nau | TEDxHSRW
recentItems.description:
What if the effort AI saves you is the very effort you need? From programming an app to avoid homework to preparing this TEDx talk with AI, Winston Nau shares a personal, humorous story about his love of shortcuts — and the moment one made him question his own thinking. He explores the difference between the effort that wastes our time and the effort that helps us grow, asking how we can embrace AI while keeping our ideas truly our own.
Filmed and edited by Fotocinema (Arkadiusz Tomala). At nine years old, Winston Nau was not dreaming of becoming a founder, developer, or AI speaker. He was dreaming of one thing: never having to pause his video games.

What started as a child’s attempt to make life easier soon became something much bigger: a fascination with coding, automation, and artificial intelligence. Winston began programming at a young age, explored AI long before ChatGPT became a global phenomenon, worked with international clients as a teenager, and now builds real-world AI solutions in Germany.

In his TEDx talk, he explores the idea of “Laziness-ology”: how the desire to avoid unnecessary effort can lead to smarter systems, better thinking, and more creative ways of working. But in a world where AI promises to make humans limitless, Winston asks an important question: Are we using AI to make thinking easier — or are we slowly forgetting how to think for ourselves? This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Listening changes what we learn | Dr. Ejura Salihu | TEDxHSRW
recentItems.description:
How much can lived experience influence research when the key decisions have already been made? Drawing on personal experience and her community-engaged work with Tai Chi Prime, Dr Ejura Yetunde Salihu explores how the timing of people’s involvement shapes what their insights can change. She invites us to rethink when we listen to the people our research, programmes and health services are intended to serve.
Filmed and edited by Fotocinema (Arkadiusz Tomala).

The Tai Chi Prime randomised trial referenced in this talk was conducted between 2016 and 2017. The findings were first published online in 2019 and later included in the June 2020 issue of The Gerontologist. Link to article: https://academic.oup.com/gerontologist/article/60/4/765/5366273 Dr. Ejura Yetunde Salihu is a health services researcher and implementation scientist whose work explores how communities, healthcare professionals, and researchers can work together to improve health outcomes and reduce health inequalities. Having lived and worked in Nigeria, the United States, and the United Kingdom, she brings a cross-cultural perspective to designing and implementing health interventions with diverse communities. At TEDxHSRW, she invites audiences to rethink how we define expertise and what it means for the future of healthcare. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Sleep to Remember: How Sleep Shapes Our Memories | Dr. Abdelrahman Rayan | TEDxHSRW
recentItems.description:
What happens to your day when we fall asleep? Neuroscientist Dr. Abdel Rayan explores how sleep helps the brain stabilize, reorganize, and integrate memories, turning the day’s experiences into tomorrow's memories. The talk shows that sleep isn't a passive break or wasted time, but an active process in which the brain uses experience to make memories last.
Filmed and edited by Fotocinema (Arkadiusz Tomala). Dr. Abdel Rayan is a neuroscientist and founder with a broad background spanning medicine, systems neuroscience, computational neuroscience, and mathematical modelling. His work explores how the brain reorganizes its activity as it moves between wakefulness and sleep, and how these changing brain states support memory consolidation.
At Radboud University and Radboudumc in Nijmegen, he uses AI and machine learning to explore sleep states across species, bridging animal and human sleep research to better understand how the brain processes experience and memories during sleep.
In his TEDx talk, Abdel invites the audience to rethink sleep: not as a passive break during the night, but as an active brain state in which the brain works with experience and memory. Drawing on neuroscience and the everyday experience of sleep, he explores how the brain stabilizes and reshapes memories, allowing parts of one day to be carried into the next. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Finding Your Voice: From Silence to Self-Expression | Dr. Antje Bothin | TEDxHSRW
recentItems.description:
In her talk, Antje explores the power of reclaiming your voice as a catalyst for personal transformation, professional growth and meaningful connection. Her work is shaped by her own journey from a once near-silent child with selective mutism to a calmly confident leader, poet and performer. She shows that assertiveness is not loudness but self‑respect in action and that no matter your past, you can rebuild, rise and reclaim your voice.
Filmed and edited by Fotocinema (Arkadiusz Tomala). Dr Antje Bothin is an assertive communication coach, trauma‑informed trainer and published author of several books based in Scotland. Originally from Germany, she writes poetry and stories about nature and wellbeing highlighting the resilience found in everyday life. Drawing on her academic background and lived experience, she helps people to find their voice, shine their light and speak with calm authority in high‑stakes conversations. As the founder of Assertive Voices, she empowers individuals to replace self‑silencing with calm confidence.
